content.comment_body: Hello, I am looking for assistance. Does anyone have an example program that can calculate the number of liters based on pulses received at an input? The display should allow entering two values: one for the number of pulses required to reach a set result, another for the basic conversion value in liters, and a final area to display the result in liters. Any help with this complex task would be appreciated. Thank you.
It would be much easier to help if you could clarify the value of a single pulse and how quickly the pulses are received.
The maximum pulse count would be 9000, with the rate being around 30 pulses per second.
You can use a fast input channel for this purpose. For instance, the I3 of the [product_name] can be connected to an Up/Down Counter block.
I'm not asking about the maximum number of pulses, but rather the value that each pulse represents. For example, is 1 pulse equal to 100 ml or 1 liter?
Do you have a link to the sensor you are using? [url]
It could be a high-speed PNP trigger sensor.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are discussing the setup for a system where a [company_name] [product_name] processes pulse inputs from a sensor to calculate and display liquid volume in liters. The discussion centers on converting pulses to volume, configuring display fields for real-time results and calibration, and program logic. Users need guidance on defining the pulse-to-volume relationship and configuring the system for dynamic value entry and display.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for an example program or step-by-step instructions on how to set up a [product_name] to count pulses, associate each pulse with a given volume in liters, and make it possible to adjust and view these values directly on the display for calibration and monitoring.
